extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and general readers interested in rhetoric and effective communication
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for judging or practicing rhetoric broadly conceived: from verbal style to gestures, political/media rhetoric, and the ethical practice of listening-rhetoric aimed at trustworthy agreement or discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening-Rhetoric (LR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listening-rhetoric (LR): the rhetor listens to the opponent so well that she can answer his questions before they’re even asked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LR is presented as a central desideratum: listening with the aim of ethical understanding and true joining of inquiry rather than merely to trick or to win. Booth labels this mode LR throughout and uses it as a model for defensible rhetorical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key test for defensible rhetoric: genuine listening
rubrics_metrics.description: The key test (chapter 3) for distinguishing defensible from indefensible rhetoric is whether genuine listening has been granted opponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should ask whether the rhetor has listened with the hope of ethical understanding or merely to defeat the opponent. Genuine listening supports trustworthy agreement; lack of it indicates rhetrickery or manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetoric as range of resources for producing effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric is the entire range of resources that human beings share for producing effects on one another: ethical, practical, emotional, and intellectual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broad definition includes not only words but gestures, facial expressions, music, art, and other symbolic skills (short of violence). When evaluating communicative acts, consider their intended effects across these domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five classical canons as evaluative dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The five lesser arts of rhetoric: inventio (discovery), dispositio (arrangement), elocutio (style), memoria (memory), and pronunciatio (delivery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these classical canons to assess rhetorical works: quality of invention/discovery of arguments, structure/organization, stylistic appropriateness, effective recall/memory where relevant, and delivery/performance. Booth notes historical shifts (e.g., inventio vs elocutio) that affect emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical distinction: rhetoric vs rhetrickery
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish ethical rhetorical practice (which seeks understanding and trustworthy agreement) from rhetrickery (deliberate deception or manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should expose shoddy or deceptive rhetoric while also recognizing rhetoric’s positive role. Consider intent, methods used to move audiences, and whether the rhetor respects truth and interlocutors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical education: protect and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Good rhetorical education should teach how to protect oneself from rhetrickery and how to practice the good kinds of rhetoric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 5 raises consequences of neglecting rhetorical training. Assess educational programs by whether they develop critical resistance to manipulative rhetoric and cultivate listening-rhetoric and ethical persuasive skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorology: deep LR aiming at discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetorology (Booth’s term) is the deepest form of LR that can yield not just diplomatic truce but discovery of new shared truths and common ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating high-level rhetorical engagement, look for work that probes rival rhetorics, seeks undisputed platforms both sides accept, and enables joint forward inquiry rather than mere compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetoric and dialectic/scientific inquiry overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric and dialectic overlap; rhetoric can be as much a mode of hard thought as dialectic and cannot be dismissed as mere ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess arguments not only for stylistic polish but for substantive discovery and reasoning; evaluate how rhetorical strategies contribute to or hinder genuine intellectual inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing rhetoric to mere style or ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware of treating rhetoric as only elocutio (style) or as 'mere rhetoric'—an appendage to real truth discovered elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should determine whether rhetorical form merely decorates pre-existing truth (Locke/Enlightenment critique) or whether rhetoric plays an integral role in discovering, shaping, or communicating knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four ends of speaking (Campbell) as evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: All the ends of speaking are reducible to four: enlighten the understanding, please the imagination, move the passions, and influence the will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these functional ends to judge speeches or communicative acts: do they clarify, engage aesthetically, emotionally move, and motivate action, and are these ends pursued ethically?

rubrics_metrics.name: Context-sensitive rhetorical evaluation across domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetorical analysis should be applied to the rhetoric of everything—philosophy, sociology, religion, science, arts—recognizing domain-specific kinds of rhetoric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating rhetoric in a particular field, account for that field’s norms and how rhetorical strategies operate there; the 'universalizing' definition requires tailoring criteria to context while recognizing common rhetorical features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and communal impact of rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of our lives, especially ethical and communal quality, depends to an astonishing degree on the quality of our rhetoric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate rhetoric in terms of its social consequences: does it reduce misunderstanding, avoid violence, build community, or does it corrode trust and civic life?

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate intent and goals of the rhetor
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetors’ goals vary from deliberate harm and 'winning at all costs' to harmonious understanding and discovery of truth; these goals affect rhetorical defensibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess not just methods but purposes: whether rhetoric is aimed at manipulation, mere victory, or shared inquiry; purpose shapes ethical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include nonverbal and artistic forms when judging rhetoric
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric includes nonverbal forms (gesture, facial expression), music and the arts; these should be counted as rhetorical when assessing persuasive effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden evaluation beyond prose/speech to consider visual, performative, and musical elements and their persuasive or communal effects (example: artistic shocking techniques).
